purpose: Independent official-series evidence for testing Randolph diesel, refined-product, freight, food, and inflation claims without using Randolph's own retrospective commentary as verification.

series.calibration_note: The series declined into July 6, then reversed sharply upward after Randolph's July 8 and July 13 diesel-focused notes. Temporal sequence alone does not establish causation or predictive superiority over crude.

series.unit: reported weekly stock change and comparison with prior five-year average
series.calibration_note: Distillate inventories rose during the week but remained materially below the five-year average, supporting a distinction between week-to-week replenishment and underlying inventory tightness.

Year-over-year energy inflation remained elevated while the July monthly energy impulse declined. Any Randolph calibration must therefore predeclare whether the forecast concerns level, year-over-year rate, month-to-month direction, or lagged pass-through.
Producer and freight measures did not move monotonically with retail diesel during July, making lag structure and transmission channel essential to any causal or predictive score.

pending_series: EIA refinery net production of distillate fuel oil
BLS detailed trucking/freight service series over March-August rather than July-only release summaries
BLS/USDA food-category series sufficient to test marine-fuel/freight-to-food pass-through
crude oil benchmark series for a predeclared comparison against gas/diesel indicator performance
interpretation_rule: This bundle contains observations, not conclusions. It cannot by itself establish that Randolph's mechanism caused an outcome, that refined products outperform crude as predictors, or that a forecast is resolved correct/incorrect.
